sections.label: MAS power to require incorporation
sections.summary: The Bill empowers MAS to require a foreign bank branch to incorporate all or part of its banking business in specified interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Bill will empower MAS to require a foreign bank branch to incorporate all or part of its banking business, where it is in the interest of the public, the bank's depositors or the domestic financial system.

sections.label: D-SIB subsidiarisation of retail operations
sections.summary: Banks with significant retail presence, defined by deposit and account thresholds, will be designated D-SIBs and required to subsidiarise retail operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In retail banking, in particular, a bank with significant retail presence – defined as having more than 3% of resident non-bank deposits, and more than 150,000 deposit accounts with balances below S$250,000 – will be designated a D-SIB and be required to subsidiarise its retail operations.

sections.label: MAS power to remove key appointment holders
sections.summary: The Bill gives MAS power to direct a bank to remove key appointment holders found not fit and proper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Bill will vest MAS with the power to direct a bank to remove key appointment holders, including its chief executive officer and deputy chief executive officer, if they are found not to be fit and proper.

sections.label: MAS approval for new places of business
sections.summary: The Bill requires banks to seek MAS approval to establish new places of business conducting certain non-banking activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Bill will also require banks to seek MAS' approval to establish new places of business where certain non-banking activities, such as money-changing and remittance business, are conducted.

sections.label: Banks must inform MAS of adverse developments
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a requirement for banks to immediately inform MAS of adverse developments that may materially affect them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, the Bill will introduce a requirement for banks to immediately inform MAS of adverse developments that may materially affect them.

sections.label: MAS power to inspect subsidiaries
sections.summary: The Bill empowers MAS to inspect the local and overseas subsidiaries of a bank incorporated in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill will empower MAS to inspect the local and overseas subsidiaries of a bank incorporated in Singapore.

sections.label: Prudential safeguards for banks
sections.summary: Prudential safeguards such as local incorporation, fit and proper ownership and auditor safe harbour will enhance MAS's ability to protect banking customers and system stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Prudential safeguards, such as empowering MAS to require a bank to incorporate locally in certain cases, only allowing fit and proper people to own significant stakes in banks, or to be a controller of the bank and providing safe harbour protection for external auditors who whistle blow, all these will enhance the ability of MAS to protect banking customers, as well as the stability and safety of the overall banking system.

sections.label: Related party transaction penalties
sections.summary: The Bill imposes new requirements and expanded penalties for related party transactions detrimental to depositors, including non-exposure transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill imposes new requirements and expanded penalties for engaging in related party transactions that are detrimental to the interests of depositors, including non-exposure transactions.

sections.label: MAS approval for business places
sections.summary: Clause 46 inserts a new section 57EA requiring banks and credit and charge card issuers to obtain MAS approval for places to conduct certain businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 46, which inserts a new section 57EA, requires banks, credit and charge card issuers to obtain approval from MAS for places where they intend to conduct certain businesses.

sections.label: P2P lending market growth
sections.summary: PwC expects the US P2P lending market to grow from US$5.5 billion in 2014 to US$150 billion in 2025, while at least five Singapore sites raised over $10 million in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), the United States (US) P2P lending market is expected to grow from US$5.5 billion in loans issued in 2014 to US$150 billion in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In Singapore, there are at least five such sites, which have collectively raised more than $10 million for their clients in 2015.

sections.label: Legitimacy of P2P platforms
sections.summary: Platforms must be legitimate and not run pyramid schemes or divert funds, as China's Ezubao turned out to be a US$7.6 billion Ponzi scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that the platforms are legitimate and are not operating pyramid schemes or funnelling funds towards uses other than what the individual lenders signed up for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This brings to mind China's Ezubao P2P lending scheme, for example, which turned out to be a US$7.6 billion Ponzi scheme.

sections.label: Industry fund and lender insurance
sections.summary: Platforms could pay part of revenues into a national fund for an industry body, and some P2P lenders like Zopa designate funds as insurance for lenders on default.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Perhaps we could explore making the platforms pay part of their revenues into a national fund to create an industry body that can help lenders pursue their claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have also seen that some P2P lenders in developed countries, such as Zopa in the UK, proactively designate a portion of their funds to provide a form of insurance to safeguard the interests of lenders in the event of a default.

sections.label: Financing channels for SMEs
sections.summary: Maintaining financing channels for SMEs is key given gathering economic dark clouds, as this could be a lifeline in tough times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Given that economic dark clouds are gathering, it is particularly key to maintain financing channels for SMEs, which are often not a target segment for major banks, as this could serve as a lifeline in tough times.

sections.label: Financial sector employment gains
sections.summary: The financial sector posted healthy employment gains, with 3,600 new jobs on a net basis over the first three quarters of 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In fact, our financial sector continued to post healthy employment gains in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have − 3,600 new jobs on a net basis over the first three quarters of 2015.

sections.label: Related party transaction provisions
sections.summary: An existing provision making bank directors jointly and severally liable for losses from credit facilities to their related parties has been repealed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, as I mentioned just now, on the related party transaction provisions, we are not just adding more rules but we have, in fact, repealed an existing provision that makes bank directors jointly and severally liable for the bank losses arising from credit facilities or exposures to their directors and their related parties.

sections.label: MAS powers over non-banking businesses
sections.summary: With this amendment, MAS will have more powers to ensure prudential standards and supervise the conduct of non-banking businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Whereas, with this amendment, MAS will now have more powers, more ability, to ensure that prudential standards are in place and to also supervise the conduct of Page: 106 non-banking businesses.

sections.label: Regulatory framework for P2P lending
sections.summary: The regulatory framework for P2P lending must address the risks posed by such platforms and balance that with allowing innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The regulatory framework for P2P lending must therefore address both the risks posed by such platforms, and strike a balance between that and allowing for innovation.

sections.label: Crowdfunding offerings to investors
sections.summary: MAS proposed facilitating securities-based crowdfunding offerings to accredited and institutional investors first, but not retail investors, who may not appreciate P2P lending risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: MAS had proposed to facilitate such securities-based crowdfunding offerings to accredited investors and institutional investors in the first instance, but not to retail investors because they may not fully appreciate the risks involved in P2P lending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For our financial system to remain stable and secure and to support economic development, the banking sector must be well-managed and remain resilient to shocks.
